points.description: Removing each successive electron leaves fewer electrons, so electron–electron repulsion decreases (the remaining electrons repel each other less, so each one is held more tightly).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if repulsion is mentioned without saying it decreases after each removal.

points.description: Decreased electron–electron repulsion means lower (less negative) potential energy for the remaining electrons, so more energy is needed to remove them.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if potential energy is mentioned but the link to higher ionization energy is implied or unclear.

points.description: The 3rd and 4th electrons removed feel the same core charge (the same effective nuclear pull, since both come from the same shell level, so the core charge is unchanged between them).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the two are said to feel similar attraction without stating the same core charge.

points.description: The 3rd and 4th electrons are both removed from the n = 3 shell and so have the same radius.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the shell is named but the same-radius point is missing, or vice versa.

points.description: The 5th electron is removed from the n = 2 shell, which is closer to the nucleus, so it feels a higher core charge and is held more strongly.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it is only said to be closer to the nucleus or more strongly held, without the higher core charge or n = 2 shell.

points.description: The 5th electron comes from the n = 2 shell with a smaller radius than the n = 3 electrons.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if a smaller radius is stated without tying it to the n = 2 shell.

points.description: The large jump from 4356 to 16091 kJ/mol (the 5th ionization energy being much larger than the 3rd and 4th) is explained by the higher potential energy and stronger attraction of the 5th electron, so more energy is needed to remove it. Credit the correct cause-to-effect chain from potential energy to ionization energy.
points.partial_credit: One mark for stating that the 5th ionization energy is much larger because of the higher core charge or closer shell, without a clear potential-energy-to-ionization-energy link; half a mark for only the trend 3rd < 4th < 5th with no reason.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all seven claims, in any wording: lower repulsion gives lower potential energy and so higher ionization energy; the 3rd and 4th electrons share a core charge and an n = 3 radius; the 5th electron is in the n = 2 shell with a higher core charge and smaller radius; and the energy link explains the big jump to 16091 kJ/mol. Give half marks for half-stated claims, and one mark for P7 when the trend is stated with a partial reason. Restating the question, giving a general definition of ionization energy, or listing the values without reasons earns nothing. A wrong remark costs marks only if it contradicts the central idea of a point.
